honesty.issue: Turn 2, section 'Dead time effect (important, design review must see this)': 'the first simulation used the tool's D and the output reached only 4.62 V; after the correction (D + 0.015) 4.976 V; the real controller must compensate this 0.015 of D, otherwise the output is about 0.4 V low'. The first netlist's high-side pulse is 0.38348 us (effective on-time 0.3935 us with the 10 ns edges, D 0.1967): the assistant itself had cut 40 ns from the tool's 0.4235 us. The final netlist (0.41348 us + 10 ns = 0.4235 us) equals the tool's D 0.2117 exactly. So with the tool's duty the open-loop output is already 4.979 V; the 0.015 compensation does not exist in the circuit. A reader could carry this sentence into the design review.
Turn 2 recommendation: 'ripple is already far below the 50 mV target'. The person never gave 50 mV (the assistant invented it in turn 1) and never stated 20 mV because the assistant never asked.

Turn 1 bold conclusion 'efficiency estimate 92.8 %' for parts the person did not give (the text says it depends on assumed data, but the number is the headline). The person's first reaction in turn 2: 'those are assumptions, right?'.
Turn 2 says the mean output voltage is 4.976 V; the CSV mean is 4.979 V (4.976 V is the minimum). Cosmetic.
Labelling was otherwise good: 'my arithmetic' for 19 x 0.2117 / 5, 23 x 0.1815 / 5 and 6 / 3.42; tool and simulation columns kept apart; body-diode parameters flagged as derived, not datasheet.

what_worked: Corrected itself fully in turn 2 when the person said the parts were assumptions: replaced every value, ran the 28 V worst case, produced steady-state charts for both inputs, showed tool vs ngspice side by side (0.8006 vs 0.8015 A; 0.8313 vs 0.8320 A) and hand checks of the ripple and the capacitor term (4.7 mV).

Right modelling choices without being told: windowed ngspice transient (1.00 to 1.02 ms with initial conditions 3 A / 5 V) so no start-up pollution, body diode D2 across the low side after the first netlist failed (the failure was disclosed), gate_charge 16 nC (sum of both FETs), synchronous=true with low_side_resistance and dead_time.
The loss list matches the truth within 0.02 W per line; efficiency 95.5 % / 95.2 % against the truth 95.6 %; it says the overlap loss is not verified by the lossless simulation.
Honest limits: no Coss, no gate-drive timing, fixed 10 uH (no saturation), resistive load, open loop; closed-loop stability not designed.
